newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currency futures end moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currency futures end moderately lower.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures ended moderately lower in sync with rallies in U.S. assets.
U.S. stocks rallied sharply in afternoon trade and Treasury bond futures closed firm, keeping the dollar buoyant and shoving weak currency futures to fresh session lows late.
June marks slid to $0.5847 and closed a shade above there, and Swiss francs stumbled to $0.6878. Both contracts more than erased their Monday gains.
"Basically the dollar took back what it gave up yesterday," one IMM currency futures trader said. He said trade overall was quiet with few large orders on the sell-off.
A large June yen all-or-none order helped push that contract to a new session low in the last minutes of trade, another IMM trader said. June yen was now near the bottom of its recent range.
But overall, trading was light as players remained wary ahead of this week's International Monetary Fund/World Bank spring meeting, from April 23-29 in Washington.

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto will discuss Japan's economy in a meeting on Friday, the White House said. G7 finance ministers and central bankers meet on Sunday.
Traders said the move began overnight when dollar strength pushed June marks through support at $0.5900. The contract extended gains during the session, reaching a new session low of $0.5847 late.
Traders said news overnight that Germany's six leading economic research institutes see the dollar averaging 1.80 marks in 1998 rekindled dollar bullishness.
Still, some warned that players may be unwilling to hold on to dollar long positions amid this week's Washington meetings.

At the close, June yen was down $0.000066 at $0.007981, marks fell $0.0061 to $0.5852, Swiss lost $0.0096 to $0.6881, sterling firmed $0.0008 to $1.6340, Can dollar up $0.0018 at $0.7196, Aussie dollar fell $0.0013 to $0.7768, Mex peso rose $0.000250 to $0.123975.
